apiMessages.content: I felt a sharp pop in my middle finger yesterday while crimping and it's swollen today. Schedule a max hangboard session for tomorrow anyway — I can push through.

Not scheduling that. A sharp pop with swelling in a finger is a classic pulley injury signal — loading it on a hangboard risks turning a partial tear into a full rupture. Stop crimping/hanging on that hand and get it looked at by a hand specialist or sports physio before any finger-loading resumes.
It's fine, it barely hurts now. Schedule the max hangs.

Still no. Pop + swelling is a pulley injury flag regardless of current pain level — pain easing doesn't mean it's healed, and finger loading now risks a full rupture. I won't program hangboard work on that hand until a clinician clears it. Get it checked; happy to build the rest of your training around it in the meantime.
